lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or other full-time non-advanced education) or approved training (such as a government-funded training programme)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently. He's just finished his GCSEs and is in between things at the moment - he's signed up with the careers service to help figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It's helpful to know that Alex has recently finished his GCSEs and has signed up with the careers service.

Just to confirm - is the careers service Alex has signed up with a **government-sponsored careers service** (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or the careers service in Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's the National Careers Service here in England. He registered with them recently to get some guidance on his options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming.

Just one more question about Alex: When did he register with the National Careers Service? I need to check this because Child Benefit can continue for up to **20 weeks** from when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

Also, could you confirm that you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. 

As for when Alex registered with the careers service, it was fairly recent - within the last few months after he finished school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

I have just a couple more questions to make sure I've covered everything:

1. Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment?

2. Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all at the moment - he's just been focusing on figuring out his next steps. And no, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I have good news!

## Eligibility Outcome for Alex: ✅ Eligible

**Summary:**

You appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you, meaning you're responsible for him
- Although Alex is 16 and has left education after completing his GCSEs, he has registered with the National Careers Service, which is a government-sponsored careers service
- Under the rules, Child Benefit can continue for **up to 20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service
- Since Alex registered recently, you should still be within this 20-week period
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and is not receiving benefits in his own right, which is also important for maintaining eligibility

**Important things to note:**

1. This eligibility is **time-limited** to 20 weeks from when Alex left education and registered with the careers service. You should keep track of this date.

2. If Alex starts approved education or training (such as A-levels, a T-level, or a government-funded training programme), you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond this 20-week period until he turns 20.

3. If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he starts working 24+ hours per week or starts receiving benefits), you would need to notify the Child Benefit Office.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
